root.claim: A deterministic multitape Turing machine multiplies two $n$-bit integers in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ time with $\kappa=2^{-182}$, disproving the $n\log n$ optimality conjecture in this model.
root.method: Build the multiplier bottom-up: power-saving tape procedures from linear exchange networks with a rank saving; a fast convolution over a polynomial ring by synthetic transforms; extension to coprime-length axes by Gaussian resampling and chirps; then the integer reduction with exact recovery and the cost accounting.
